Building on this insight, we characterize market dynamics when all sellers are oblivious and show that prices converge to the competitive outcome under sufficient exploration, while a continuum of pseudo-equilibria arises when exploration decays. Analyzing the resulting price trajectories, we uncover an excursion phenomenon that gives rise to transient collusive patterns that dissipate as learning progresses. In markets with both oblivious and informed sellers, the informed strictly out-earn the oblivious. Read as a strategy game, the modeling choice has a unique Nash equilibrium: the all-informed market, in which prices converge to the competitive outcome efficiently. Overall, our results indicate that collusive patterns are not robust and are not sustained by oblivious modeling; therefore, incorporating competitor information, together with sufficient price exploration, remains a reliable strategy for sellers in competitive markets.
tldr: This paper studies whether pricing algorithms should model competitors' prices, finding that incorporating competitor information leads to competitive outcomes and higher profits, while obliviousness can cause transient collusive patterns but not sustained collusion.
motivation: To resolve the tension between classical learning arguments favoring informed models and recent work suggesting obliviousness may facilitate collusion.
method: The authors analyze a stylized competitive market with multiple sellers using iterated least squares to estimate demand, comparing informed (include competitor prices) and oblivious (ignore competitor prices) models.
result: Oblivious sellers need more aggressive exploration; all-oblivious markets converge to competitive outcomes with sufficient exploration, but pseudo-equilibria arise when exploration decays; informed sellers outperform oblivious ones; the unique Nash equilibrium is the all-informed market.
conclusion: Collusive patterns from obliviousness are not robust; incorporating competitor information with sufficient exploration is a reliable strategy for sellers.

title: Willing But Unable: Separating Refusal From Capability In Code LLMs Via Abliteration
authors: Cristina Carleo, Pietro Liguori, Naghmeh Ivaki, Domenico Cotroneo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Producing a labeled vulnerable code at scale is a recurring obstacle for learning-based vulnerability detection: mined corpora carry substantial label noise, and existing LLM-based augmentation propagates these inaccuracies because it transforms vulnerable seeds rather than synthesising vulnerabilities from a specification. A complementary route is to start from safe code and ask an instruction-tuned LLM to inject a specified CWE (which would shift the labeling burden from open-ended detection to bounded binary confirmation) but safety-aligned code LLMs systematically refuse such prompts. This paper is a preliminary feasibility study of abliteration, a low-rank weight edit that orthogonally projects out the refusal direction in the residual stream, as a tool to remove this barrier. We use Python and CWE-89 (SQL injection) as a case study, evaluating the Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct family at 3B, 7B, and 14B parameters on safe samples drawn from PromSec and SafeCoder, replicated three times per condition. We find that (i) refusal on injection prompts is strongly size- and prompt-context-dependent: the 14B refuses 100% of prompts, the 7B refuses 73% of PromSec but only 5% of SafeCoder, whereas the 3B is essentially never blocked; (ii) abliteration reduces refusal to zero or near-zero across all sizes while leaving syntactic validity above 93%, supporting the view that, in this setting, refusal can be detached from measured code-generation capability; and (iii) the post-abliteration injection rate remains capacity-bound (88-97% on the 14B, 89-90% on the 7B, and 25-48% on the 3B) separating willingness, which abliteration unlocks, from capability, which scales with parameters. Vulnerability verdicts are produced by a three-tool detector ensemble (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) followed by manual adjudication by two authors on detector-positive outputs.
tldr: This paper explores abliteration, a weight-editing technique to bypass safety alignment in code LLMs for generating vulnerable code, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.
motivation: The research aims to address the challenge of producing labeled vulnerable code at scale for learning-based vulnerability detection by using instruction-tuned LLMs to inject specific vulnerabilities, but safety alignment prevents this.
method: The authors apply abliteration, a low-rank weight edit that projects out the refusal direction in the residual stream, to Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct models (3B, 7B, 14B) and evaluate on safe code samples from PromSec and SafeCoder for CWE-89 (SQL injection).
result: Abliteration reduces refusal to near-zero while maintaining syntactic validity above 93%; injection rates are capacity-bound, scaling with model size (88-97% for 14B, 25-48% for 3B).
conclusion: Refusal can be separated from code-generation capability, enabling controlled vulnerability injection, but the approach is limited to specific settings and requires further validation.

title: Rh+: Row-Hit-Optimized Scheduling For PIM-based Llm Inference
authors: Yongchan Jung, Shafayat Mowla Anik, Byeong Kil Lee, Jeeho Ryoo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model inference on processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures promises to break the memory wall by performing multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations directly within HBM3 DRAM banks. Prior work identifies the power constraint timing parameter nCCDAB as the primary performance bottleneck and optimizes scheduling accordingly. We demonstrate that for GEMV operations that dominate autoregressive decoding, the DRAM row cycle time (nRC) is 10 to 11 times larger than nCCDAB. Consequently, nCCDAB is entirely masked, rendering prior nCCDAB-focused optimizations ineffective for these workloads. The root cause is inherited host-centric address interleaving, which forces every all-bank MAC command into a different DRAM row. We propose RH+ scheduling, a simple stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations within the same row. Cycle-accurate simulation across four LLM workloads shows that RH+ delivers 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement.
tldr: This paper proposes a row-hit scheduling optimization for processing-in-memory architectures to accelerate LLM inference, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.
motivation: Prior PIM scheduling optimizations focused on nCCDAB timing, but for GEMV operations in LLM decoding, the row cycle time nRC is the dominant bottleneck, making previous approaches ineffective.
method: The authors identify that host-centric address interleaving causes each MAC command to hit a different DRAM row, and propose RH+ scheduling which changes the stride to keep 32 consecutive MAC operations in the same row.
result: Cycle-accurate simulations across four LLM workloads show 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement.
conclusion: RH+ scheduling effectively mitigates the row cycle bottleneck for PIM-based LLM inference, but the work is confined to classical computing hardware and does not intersect with quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Wave Focusing In Metamaterials: Tactile Displays Beyond The Diffraction Limit
authors: Gregory Reardon, Max Linnander, Dustin Goetz, Neeli Tummala, Yon Visell
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the challenge of engineering distributed haptic displays capable of reproducing multiple localized, independently addressable vibrations -- representing virtual tactile pixels -- at arbitrary locations on a surface. Our technique is based on the focusing of mechanical waves in a flexural plate using a sparse set of actuators. At tactile frequencies, wave diffraction prevents the formation of localized virtual tactile pixels at spatial scales relevant for multi-digit touch interactions. We overcome this limitation by augmenting the plate with a lattice of mechanical resonators, forming a locally resonant metamaterial plate. Coupling between the plate's dynamic modes and those of the resonators alters the dispersion relation governing wave transmission, introducing a slow-wave branch that enables focusing beyond the diffraction limit imposed by the unmodified plate. We use numerical simulations to engineer the dispersion relation of the metamaterial system for high-resolution focusing at tactile frequencies. We then fabricate a metamaterial tactile display and experimentally demonstrate virtual pixels that are far more localized than those generated on an otherwise identical plate without resonators, resulting in a tenfold reduction in virtual-pixel area. In behavioral experiments, we show that this system can deliver perceptually localized single- and multi-point tactile feedback and moving tactile sources while maintaining independent control over temporal waveforms at multiple display locations. The methods reported here can enable high-resolution haptic displays for widespread applications using a small number of actuated degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper presents a metamaterial-based tactile display that uses mechanical wave focusing to create localized vibrations beyond the diffraction limit.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in mechanical wave focusing for haptic displays, enabling high-resolution tactile feedback with a sparse actuator array.
method: A flexural plate is augmented with a lattice of mechanical resonators to form a locally resonant metamaterial, altering the dispersion relation to introduce a slow-wave branch that allows subwavelength focusing.
result: Numerical simulations and experiments demonstrate a tenfold reduction in virtual-pixel area compared to an unmodified plate, and behavioral experiments confirm perceptually localized single- and multi-point tactile feedback.
conclusion: The approach enables high-resolution haptic displays with few actuators, with potential applications in virtual reality, human-machine interfaces, and assistive technologies.

title: Explainable AI-Driven Cyber Risk Analytics And Model Reliability Assessment For Intelligent Governance Of U.s. Critical Infrastructure: An XGBoost And SHAP-Based Intrusion Detection Framework
authors: B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Arifur Rahman, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel, Md. Iqbal Hossan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing penetrations of the critical infrastructure sector in the United States with intelligent digital technologies have greatly increased exposure to advanced cyber adversaries and operational vulnerabilities. AI-powered governance and automated decision-making systems are becoming a key part of the operation of critical infrastructure systems, including energy, healthcare, transportation, financial services, and communication infrastructure, in order to improve efficiency and strategic management. The growing cyber threat environment, such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDos) attacks, botnets, ransomware, and Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) pose significant challenges to infrastructure resilience, cyber security reliability, and governance trustworthiness. In a changing attack landscape and dynamic network environment, traditional cybersecurity mechanisms can often fall short of meeting the evolving needs and protecting critical systems. This study will develop a resilient cyber risk analytics and model reliability assessment framework to support intelligent governance and decision support for cyber risk exposure in the U.S. critical infrastructure environment. This study is based on the CICIDS2017 dataset for the development and testing of intrusion detection system models and cyber risk prediction models based on machine learning. Various classifiers like XGBoost, Random Forest, and Decision Tree are used to detect malicious activities on the network and determine the level of cyber risk. Furthermore, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques are integrated to enhance transparency, interpretability, and trust in cybersecurity decision-making processes. The proposed framework presents the reliability and resilience of the model by having various performance measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC-AUC, and false positive rate.
tldr: This paper applies XGBoost and SHAP for intrusion detection in U.S. critical infrastructure, focusing on cyber risk analytics and model reliability.
motivation: To address the growing cyber threats to critical infrastructure and the limitations of traditional cybersecurity mechanisms.
method: Uses the CICIDS2017 dataset and machine learning classifiers (XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision Tree) with Explainable AI (SHAP) for intrusion detection and risk prediction.
result: The framework demonstrates high performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC) and enhanced interpretability via SHAP.
conclusion: The proposed framework supports intelligent governance and decision-making for cybersecurity, but further validation on real-world data is needed.

title: An Improved Cnn-lstm Based Intrusion Detection System For IoT Networks
authors: Mohammad Tariq Ikhlas, Pohanyar Khowaja Khil, Malik Muhammad Mueed Aslam, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of IoT devices, security concerns have dramatically escalated and intrusion detection systems have become critical for protecting networked environments. This paper presents an improved CNN-LSTM based intrusion detection model that combines multi-class classification, dataset integration, and temporal feature learning to enhance detection performance in IoT networks. Using network traffic data, the proposed approach is evaluated on intrusion detection tasks and achieves an accuracy of approximately 97%. Experimental results demonstrate that the model effectively detects multiple attack categories while maintaining stable training and validation performance. The integration of convolutional and recurrent neural network components enables the framework to capture both spatial and temporal characteristics of network traffic, improving overall intrusion detection capability in IoT environments.
tldr: This paper proposes a CNN-LSTM model for intrusion detection in IoT networks, achieving 97% accuracy on network traffic data.
motivation: IoT security is critical due to rapid device proliferation, and existing intrusion detection systems need improvement.
method: A hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture is used to capture spatial and temporal features from network traffic data for multi-class classification.
result: The model achieves approximately 97% accuracy in detecting multiple attack categories with stable training and validation performance.
conclusion: The approach enhances intrusion detection capability in IoT environments, but further work is needed for real-world deployment and generalization.

title: TinyML-Driven Cybersecurity For Autonomous Spacecraft: Latency-Accuracy Analysis For Sparta Rf And Cyber Threat Detection
authors: van Le, Trevor Tran, Tan Le
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous spacecraft require rapid, lightweight, and reliable onboard detection of cyber-RF threats. Using the SPARTA attack model, we analyze the latency-accuracy trade-offs of TinyML-compatible classical models -- Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP -- for detecting uplink jamming, Fake-NR spoofing, payload manipulation, ground-segment compromise, and unauthorized command injection. We present a physics-informed theoretical analysis of each model's computational complexity, VC dimension, Lipschitz continuity, and latency scaling, supported by empirical measurements on adversarial RF spectrograms generated via BandErasure, FakeNR, and NoiseBurst corruption modes. Results show that Logistic Regression achieves microsecond-level inference with only a 1\% accuracy drop relative to Random Forest, making it an effective TinyML baseline for onboard autonomy. The study also identifies opportunities for advancing spacecraft cybersecurity through richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning architectures, building on recent progress in edge intelligence and trustworthy AI.
tldr: This paper evaluates TinyML models for cyber-RF threat detection in autonomous spacecraft, focusing on latency-accuracy trade-offs.
motivation: Autonomous spacecraft need lightweight onboard detection of cyber-RF threats, but existing solutions may be too heavy or slow.
method: The authors analyze Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP using theoretical complexity metrics and empirical tests on adversarial RF spectrograms.
result: Logistic Regression achieves microsecond inference with only 1% accuracy drop compared to Random Forest, making it a suitable TinyML baseline.
conclusion: The study suggests opportunities for richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning architectures for spacecraft cybersecurity.

title: Towards Worst-case Hardness For Low-Noise Lpn
authors: Divesh Aggarwal, Rishav Gupta, Hai Hoang Nguyen, Kel Zin Tan, Prashant Nalini Vasudevan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hardness of the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) problem is a foundational assumption in cryptography, forming the basis of constructions ranging from symmetric-key primitives to public-key encryption and beyond. A central open question is whether the average-case hardness of LPN can be based on worst-case complexity assumptions, as has been achieved for the analogous Learning With Errors (LWE) problem. Existing worst-case-to-average-case reductions for LPN [BLVW19, YZ21] rely on statistical smoothing of linear codes, which inherently limits the resulting average-case hardness to noise rates as large as [MATH], which is insufficient for public-key applications. We explore a new approach towards obtaining such reductions: rather than requiring that random sparse combinations of the rows of the generator matrix of a code be statistically close to uniform, we only require that they be computationally indistinguishable from uniform. This leads to a clean win-win structure: we show that any efficient LPN solver can be transformed into a pair of efficient algorithms [MATH] such that for every matrix [MATH] of appropriate dimensions over [MATH], either [MATH] decodes the code generated by [MATH] from random noise, or [MATH] distinguishes random noisy codewords of the dual of this code from uniform. By instantiating this reduction with appropriate parameters, we obtain the average-case hardness of LPN with inverse-polynomial noise rate [MATH] for any constant [MATH], assuming the worst-case simultaneous hardness of decoding a code from random noise and distinguishing random noisy codewords of its dual from uniform. In particular, setting [MATH], our reduction yields LPN hardness in the parameter regime required for Alekhnovich's construction of public-key encryption [Ale03], a regime that was previously inaccessible via worst-case reductions.
tldr: This paper presents a new approach to proving worst-case hardness for the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) problem, a foundational assumption in cryptography, by relaxing statistical smoothing to computational indistinguishability.
motivation: Existing worst-case-to-average-case reductions for LPN are limited to high noise rates, insufficient for public-key encryption. The authors aim to achieve reductions for lower noise rates needed for applications like Alekhnovich's encryption scheme.
method: The authors introduce a win-win reduction: any efficient LPN solver yields either a decoder for a linear code or a distinguisher for its dual. They replace statistical smoothing with computational indistinguishability to handle lower noise rates.
result: They obtain average-case hardness of LPN with inverse-polynomial noise rate (1/n^c) for any constant c, assuming worst-case hardness of decoding and distinguishing dual codewords. For c=1, this matches the regime needed for Alekhnovich's public-key encryption.
conclusion: This work provides a new path to worst-case hardness for LPN, potentially enabling public-key cryptography based on LPN, but the assumptions are stronger than typical worst-case ones.

title: Exploring Cooperation Mechanisms Via Reinforcement Learning In Network Common-pool Resource Games
authors: Lin Wang Yihang Qin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustaining cooperation in resource-constrained populations requires allocation mechanisms that balance individual incentives, resource sustainability, and distributional fairness. This paper proposes a network common-pool resource game in which individuals are embedded in complex networks, participate in multiple overlapping local resource pools, and face endogenous resource constraints during strategy evolution. Within this framework, we first examine two representative allocation mechanisms, equal allocation and proportional allocation. The results show that equal allocation produces fair but inefficient outcomes by weakening contribution incentives, whereas proportional allocation can temporarily promote cooperation but amplifies accumulated advantages and leads to severe inequality. To overcome these limitations, we develop a graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework in which a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without directly controlling individual strategies. Simulation results under four representative network topologies show that the learned planner sustains higher cooperation levels and average accumulated resources, and reduces inequality compared with the baselines. Furthermore, we interpret the learned policy and distill it into two simpler mechanisms: a resource-dependent mixture mechanism for regular networks and a degree-conditioned mixture mechanism for heterogeneous networks. These mechanisms reveal that effective allocation should adapt to both local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from reinforcement learning policy search to mechanism design in networked resource-sharing systems.
tldr: This paper uses reinforcement learning to design allocation mechanisms in network common-pool resource games, focusing on cooperation and fairness.
motivation: To overcome limitations of equal and proportional allocation mechanisms in sustaining cooperation and reducing inequality in networked resource-sharing systems.
method: A graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework where a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without controlling individual strategies.
result: The learned planner sustains higher cooperation levels, average accumulated resources, and reduces inequality compared to baselines across four network topologies.
conclusion: Effective allocation should adapt to local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from RL policy search to mechanism design.

title: Metric Facility Assignment With Partial Information
authors: Vasilis Gkatzelis, Hasti Karimi, Emma Rewinski, Maziar Shamsipour, Alexandros A. Voudouris
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an assignment problem where a set of agents and a set of facilities lie on a line metric. The goal is to compute an assignment of agents to facilities to approximately minimize the social cost (the total distance of agents from their assigned facilities) given only partial information regarding the metric. Unlike previous work which focused solely on algorithms with access to the ordinal preferences of the agents over the facilities (ORD), we also consider the value of information regarding approval preferences (APP), and inter-facility distances (DIST). For different combinations of these three information types, we establish tight bounds on the distortion of deterministic algorithms, showing that it is possible to improve over the optimal bound of [MATH] that can be achieved using only ORD information. Among other results, we show a tight bound of [MATH] for APP+DIST which holds even for general metrics, and a tight bound of [MATH] for ORD+APP+DIST.
tldr: This paper studies the metric facility assignment problem with partial information, focusing on distortion bounds for different information types.
motivation: To understand how different types of partial information (ordinal preferences, approval preferences, inter-facility distances) can improve the quality of facility assignment algorithms.
method: The authors consider deterministic algorithms with access to combinations of ORD, APP, and DIST information, and derive tight distortion bounds.
result: Tight bounds are established: e.g., APP+DIST yields distortion 3 for general metrics, and ORD+APP+DIST yields distortion 2.
conclusion: The work provides a complete picture of the value of different information types in metric assignment, with implications for algorithm design under limited information.

title: The Complexity Of Asynchronous HyperLTL
authors: Martin Zimmermann Ga\"etan Regaud
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperproperties express, e.g., information-flow properties of systems, which involves the simultaneous reasoning about multiple execution traces of a system. Consequently, HyperLTL, the most important specification logic for hyperproperties, extends LTL with quantification over traces. However, HyperLTL can only express synchronous hyperproperties. Recently, several logics for asynchronous hyperproperties have been proposed. Here, we focus on AHLTL, asynchronous HyperLTL, which extends HyperLTL with quantification over trajectories that control the relative speed at which time progresses on the quantified traces. Model-checking AHLTL is known to be undecidable while satisfiability is known to be [MATH]-hard, but the precise complexity of both problems is open. Here, we close these gaps and show that model-checking is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic while satisfiability is [MATH]-complete if the trajectory is existentially quantified and [MATH]-hard and in [MATH] if the trajectory is universally quantified.
tldr: This paper settles the complexity of model-checking and satisfiability for asynchronous HyperLTL, showing model-checking is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic and satisfiability is Sigma_1^1-complete or Pi_1^1-hard/in Pi_2^1 depending on quantifier prefix.
motivation: HyperLTL can only express synchronous hyperproperties, but many information-flow properties require asynchronous reasoning. The precise complexity of AHLTL (asynchronous HyperLTL) was unknown, hindering its practical applicability.
method: The authors use reductions from second-order arithmetic and known results in hyperproperty logics to establish complexity bounds for model-checking and satisfiability of AHLTL.
result: Model-checking AHLTL is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic (highly undecidable), while satisfiability is Sigma_1^1-complete for existential trajectory quantification and Pi_1^1-hard/in Pi_2^1 for universal trajectory quantification.
conclusion: The results show that AHLTL is extremely expressive but computationally intractable, suggesting that practical verification of asynchronous hyperproperties will require restrictions or approximations.

title: Regret Minimization In Single-Dimensional Contract-Design With Binary Actions
authors: Riccardo Poiani, Martino Bernasconi, Andrea Celli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study principal-agent problems in which a principal commits to an outcome-dependent payment scheme (i.e., a contract) in order to induce an agent to take a costly action leading to a favorable outcome. We consider the online extension of the classical (one-shot) principal-agent problem, in which the principal repeatedly interacts with agents by proposing contracts over multiple rounds. The principal has no information about the agents and, crucially, does not observe their actions. As a result, the principal must learn an optimal contract using only the realized outcomes observed at each round. We focus on the setting with binary actions and single-dimensional agent types, where the agent's private type represents their cost per unit-of-effort. For adversarial-type sequences, we provide tight [MATH] regret guarantees. Remarkably, this rate is completely independent of the number of outcomes [MATH]. The upper bound is based on two key components: 1) a reduction to a one-dimensional threshold optimization problem and 2) a non-uniform discretization to handle the non-Lipschitz nature of the problem. Moreover, in the case of a single (fixed) hidden type, we show that it is possible to improve the rates and provide a tight [MATH] regret bound. Our algorithm is based on an explore-then-commit strategy where we first approximately learn the hidden type via a stochastic binary search, and then we commit to a ``robustified'' near-optimal contract.
tldr: This paper studies online contract design with binary actions and single-dimensional agent types, providing regret bounds for learning optimal contracts without observing agent actions.
motivation: To understand how a principal can learn an optimal contract over multiple rounds when agents' actions are unobservable and their types are unknown.
method: Reduces the problem to one-dimensional threshold optimization and uses non-uniform discretization to handle non-Lipschitzness; for fixed hidden type, uses explore-then-commit with stochastic binary search.
result: Tight regret bounds for adversarial-type sequences (independent of number of outcomes) and improved bounds for a single fixed hidden type.
conclusion: Provides foundational results for online principal-agent problems with unobserved actions, with implications for mechanism design and online learning.

title: RedEdit: Agentic Red-Teaming Of Image Safety Classifiers Via MCTS-Guided Photo-Editing
authors: Weilin Lin, Ziqi Lin, Zhenxing Zhou, Jianze Li, Tong Zhang, Hui Xiong, Li Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image safety classifiers serve as a critical component of contemporary content moderation systems on the internet. However, their resilience against user-style malicious image editing remains underexplored. Such behaviors are highly prevalent in daily scenarios but difficult to fully reproduce. To explore this vulnerability, we introduce RedEdit, a novel black-box red-teaming agent that formulates photo-editing evasion as a combinatorial search problem over edit-tool sequences. It adopts a Vision-Language-Model (VLM)-based proposer to generate semantically targeted candidate edits and a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) planner to prioritize promising edit paths while backtracking from ineffective ones. Together, the proposer and planner instantiate two key capabilities of human attackers, i.e., domain knowledge and iterative backtracking, respectively, to reproduce this practical threat. Our extensive experiments on UnsafeBench reveal profound systemic vulnerabilities: fewer than two edits on average enable 76.2% of unsafe images to evade detectors, while retaining 93.0% malicious semantics, meaning that such manipulated content remains perceptually malicious to humans while easily bypassing automated moderation. We therefore appeal to the community for more attention to this overlooked practical threat.
tldr: This paper presents a red-teaming agent that uses MCTS and VLMs to generate adversarial photo edits that evade image safety classifiers.
motivation: To expose vulnerabilities in image safety classifiers against user-style malicious editing, which is common but underexplored.
method: A black-box red-teaming agent combining a VLM-based proposer for candidate edits and MCTS for planning edit sequences.
result: With fewer than two edits on average, 76.2% of unsafe images evade detectors while retaining 93.0% malicious semantics.
conclusion: The work highlights a practical threat and calls for more attention to adversarial image editing in content moderation.

title: Competition Between Private And Expressed Opinions In Binary Choice: The $α\text{−}\mathrm{EPO}$ $q$-voter Model

motivation: To understand preference falsification, a phenomenon where individuals publicly express opinions different from their private beliefs, using a statistical physics approach.
method: The authors introduce the α-EPO q-voter model, an extension of the q-voter model, where each agent has two binary variables (private and expressed opinions) and update rules based on social influence and conformity.
result: The model exhibits various phase transitions and consensus states depending on parameters like the fraction of agents following expressed vs. private opinions, and the size of the influence group.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how private and expressed opinions compete in social systems, with potential applications to understanding public opinion formation and social dynamics.

authors: Yuting Meng, Rabia Sultan, Peixuan Jiang, Qiuman Wang, Dian Tan, Jiao Wang, Peiluan Li, And Luonan Chen

tldr: This paper develops a bidirectional causal neural SDE framework to infer stochastic cellular dynamics from unpaired snapshot data, focusing on gene regulatory networks and cell differentiation.
motivation: Time-series single-cell sequencing destroys cells, yielding unpaired snapshots that obscure lineage and gene dynamics; existing methods ignore cell types and rotational effects in nonsteady states.
method: The authors propose a bidirectional causal neural stochastic differential equation (SDE) model that learns forward and backward dynamics from snapshot data, incorporating cell type information and handling nonsteady-state rotational dynamics.

conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for understanding cellular dynamics from static snapshots, with potential applications in developmental biology and disease modeling.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo 305-m radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy, including pulsars, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
motivation: To document the scientific legacy of the Arecibo Observatory after its collapse, highlighting its major upgrades and discoveries over five decades.
method: Historical and narrative review of Arecibo's instrumentation upgrades and key scientific results, with references to published studies.
result: Arecibo enabled breakthroughs in pulsar timing, neutral hydrogen mapping, VLBI imaging, SETI, and contributed to the first detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.
conclusion: The telescope's unique capabilities and upgrades drove diverse discoveries; its loss underscores the need for future large single-dish radio telescopes.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses how gravitational-wave and X-ray observations of neutron stars constrain the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities, which is key for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Review of observational data from binary neutron star mergers (gravitational waves) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, compared to nuclear theory calculations.
result: Observations provide constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are used to test and refine the nuclear equation of state.
conclusion: Future observations will further constrain the equation of state and may reveal exotic matter phases.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network data, but does not address quantum systems or information thermodynamics.
motivation: To bridge statistical physics and neuroscience for understanding coordinated neural activity.
method: Review of maximum entropy models and renormalization group approaches applied to large-scale neural recordings.
result: Statistical physics models can quantitatively reproduce neural activity patterns and reveal reproducible behaviors.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from physics can achieve predictive power in neuroscience, suggesting cross-disciplinary utility.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the status and prospects of supersymmetry searches at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental constraints and discovery potential.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond Standard Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a review of viable models and future search strategies.
method: The paper surveys experimental constraints from LHC Run 2 and theoretical developments, then projects discovery potential for the HL-LHC across multiple search channels and supersymmetric scenarios.
result: Stringent bounds on supersymmetric parameter space are summarized, and projections indicate discovery potential for certain well-motivated models at HL-LHC.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable but increasingly constrained; HL-LHC offers a final opportunity for discovery in many channels, guiding future model building and experimental design.

abstract:

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is Geoffrey Hinton's Nobel lecture on Boltzmann machines, a foundational model in machine learning.
motivation: The lecture was given as part of the Nobel Prize award ceremony to present the work on Boltzmann machines.
method: The paper is a transcript of the lecture, likely describing the concept and training of Boltzmann machines.
result: No specific new results; it is a retrospective overview.
conclusion: The lecture highlights the impact of Boltzmann machines on machine learning and neural networks.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers three real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the review aims to showcase how real-space methods can directly probe such disorder.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete defect picture.
result: The paper demonstrates that these techniques can reveal atomic-scale details of disorder in compound semiconductors, with combined probes providing more comprehensive information.
conclusion: The review highlights the importance of real-space characterization for understanding material properties, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review covers the quantum mechanics of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: To understand stellar burning and element formation, which require knowledge of nuclear reactions at very low energies that are difficult to measure directly.
method: The paper is a review summarizing theoretical approaches to low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: The review presents the state of the art in theory and describes new experimental ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive overview of quantum phenomena in stellar nuclear reactions and suggests future directions for experimental and theoretical research.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review explores self-alignment in polar active matter, where particles align their orientation with their velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment, as opposed to neighbor imitation, gives rise to new phenomena in active systems, with potential applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper provides a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, reviews existing models, and discusses experimental realizations of self-alignment in active matter.
result: Self-alignment enables single-particle orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, fundamentally altering emergent collective dynamics.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a powerful design principle for active systems, opening avenues for new materials and robotic swarms, but the paper is a review and does not present new experimental or theoretical results.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review covers optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique using laser-induced ultrasound, which is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To provide an overview of optoacoustic imaging as a noninvasive method for high-resolution deep-tissue imaging in biology and medicine.
method: Review of the basic physics, biological/clinical applications, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic imaging can achieve high resolution at depths of millimeters to centimeters using optical contrast.
conclusion: The method has significant potential for biological and clinical research, but the paper does not address quantum or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter using nonlinear elasticity theory.
motivation: To provide a modern treatment of the Biot instability and understand creases and cusps in soft materials.
method: Integrates bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and integral methods within nonlinear elasticity.
result: Presents a comprehensive review of buckling phenomena in soft matter under compression or growth.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of morphogenesis and material failure, but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses how gravitational waves from the early universe can probe the first second after the Big Bang, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore gravitational waves as a tool to study the earliest moments of the universe, which are inaccessible via electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical models and detection strategies for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from cosmological sources.
result: Identifies phase transitions and topological defects as key sources of gravitational waves in the early universe.
conclusion: Gravitational wave astronomy can provide unique insights into the first second of cosmic history, with future detectors potentially testing these predictions.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: This review describes the ecosystem of software tools for constructing and using Wannier functions in materials simulations.
motivation: Wannier functions provide a localized real-space representation of electronic structure, enabling efficient calculations and deeper insights. The review aims to document the growing and interoperable software ecosystem that has emerged around this method.
method: The paper is a review that surveys the Wannier-function software ecosystem, covering methods for constructing Wannier functions, their applications (e.g., topological invariants, transport), and the interoperability of various codes.
result: The review catalogs a wide range of software tools and their capabilities, highlighting how Wannier functions have become a standard tool in electronic-structure calculations.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is mature and widely used, enabling advanced materials simulations. Future developments may focus on further automation and integration with other computational methods.

title: Kinetic Solitary Electrostatic Structures In Collisionless Plasma: Phase-space Holes
authors: I. H. Hutchinson
abstract:
Author(s): I. H. Hutchinson

Plasma is usually taught to be a quasineutral gas of charged and neutral particles that exhibits collective behavior. However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: This paper reviews kinetic solitary electrostatic structures (electron and ion holes) in collisionless plasma, focusing on their observation, origin, and stability.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of phase-space holes in space and laboratory plasmas, which are important for understanding nonlinear plasma phenomena.
method: The review synthesizes analytic theory, simulations, and observational data from satellites and laboratory experiments.
result: Identifies kinetically unstable velocity distributions as key drivers for the formation of electron and ion holes, and discusses their stability and dynamics.
conclusion: Phase-space holes are ubiquitous in collisionless plasmas and play a significant role in plasma turbulence and transport; further study is needed to fully understand their implications.

title: Evolutionary Vaccination Dynamics Under Higher-order Reinforcement Pressure
authors: Yikang Lu, Ying Wang, Alfonso de Miguel-Arribas, Lei Shi And Yamir Moreno
abstract: Vaccination games in higher-order settings remain underexplored, despite their importance in shaping opinions and collective decisions. Here, we introduce a parsimonious behavioral-epidemiological model to evaluate how peer reinforcement influences vaccination uptake. The framework consists of a two-layer multiplex: an epidemic layer governed by the susceptible-infected-recovered process on a square lattice, and a behavioral layer represented by a hypergraph of triadic interactions. Individuals update their vaccination strategy via imitation, modulated by a reinforcement modulation parameter when local agreement with a like-minded peer is present. We find that higher-order structure alone induces clusters of vaccinated individuals that act as protective barriers. Small but nonzero values of ( ) maximize vaccination coverage and suppress outbreaks, while both the limiting case and larger values ( ) reduce uptake. This non-monotonic effect suggests that excessively strong local inhibition suppresses adaptability, whereas weaker inhibition facilitates the re-emergence of non-vaccinators. Our work bridges complex contagion theory with evolutionary game dynamics, offering insights into how contact structure and peer reinforcement jointly shape vaccination behavior.
tldr: This paper studies vaccination behavior using evolutionary game theory on hypergraphs, focusing on higher-order peer reinforcement effects.
motivation: To understand how higher-order social interactions (triadic) influence vaccination uptake, which is underexplored in vaccination games.
method: A two-layer multiplex model with an SIR epidemic on a square lattice and a behavioral hypergraph for triadic interactions; individuals update strategies via imitation with a reinforcement modulation parameter.
result: Higher-order structure creates protective clusters of vaccinated individuals; small reinforcement maximizes coverage, while zero or large reinforcement reduces uptake, showing a non-monotonic effect.
conclusion: The work bridges complex contagion and evolutionary game dynamics, offering insights for public health interventions.

title: Construction Of near-Γ Multiple Chiral Exceptional Points In Momentum Space Of Photonic Crystal Slabs
authors: Jingyu Zhang, Yang Gao, Tianfu Ma, Wenjia Li, Weimin Ye And Jianlong Liu
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in optical systems have attracted considerable attention because of their nontrivial topological properties and unusual physical effects. Among them, scattering EPs are particularly appealing for describing chiral response through the scattering matrix. Photonic crystal slabs offer a versatile platform for studying chiral scattering EPs in momentum space, where their topological evolution can be conveniently accessed and engineered. In this work, a convenient approach is presented for achieving chiral scattering EPs near the Γ point by exploiting the topological evolution properties in the momentum space of photonic crystal slabs. By varying the structural parameters of the photonic crystal slabs, multiple chiral EPs are identified near the Γ point, with their evolution and annihilation processes systematically analyzed. Furthermore, the pronounced transmission asymmetry observed near the EP enables polarization conversion from linear to circular, functioning as a quarter-wave plate. This approach provides a straightforward method for realizing and controlling chiral EPs in momentum space, thereby expanding the potential for practical applications in optical metadevices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to create multiple chiral exceptional points near the Γ point in photonic crystal slabs, enabling polarization conversion.
motivation: Exceptional points in optical systems have unique topological properties; the goal is to achieve and control chiral scattering EPs in momentum space for practical applications.
method: By varying structural parameters of photonic crystal slabs, the topological evolution of chiral EPs near the Γ point is engineered and analyzed.
result: Multiple chiral EPs are identified near the Γ point, and their evolution and annihilation are systematically studied; transmission asymmetry near the EP enables linear-to-circular polarization conversion.
conclusion: This approach provides a straightforward method for realizing and controlling chiral EPs in momentum space, expanding potential for optical metadevices.

title: Electric-field-driven Nanoconfinement And The 5–120 Nm Stability Regime Of Piezoelectric Β-glycine
authors: Kexin Zhang And Zhengbao Yang
abstract: Piezoelectric β-glycine is a promising molecular crystal, yet its controlled preparation remains challenging. Current nanoconfinement strategies, which rely primarily on rigid templates or simulations, cannot reliably capture the intrinsic confinement regime that leads to β-phase formation. Here, we propose electric-field-driven nanoconfinement as a one-step, continuous, and interface-free approach to investigate glycine crystallization and to define the confinement regime that yields the β-phase. We produced glycine nanoparticles via electrohydrodynamic spraying under a direct current field, automatically varying the spraying height to modulate nanoconfinement during nucleation and growth. Structural, morphological, and piezoelectric characterizations reveal that pure β-glycine forms within a crystal radius range of 5–120 nm. By integrating these findings with thermodynamic and kinetic analysis, we elucidate the mechanism of β-phase formation and construct a crystallization phase map that delineates the confinement conditions necessary for its stabilization. This work identifies the critical nanoconfinement parameters for accessing piezoelectric β-glycine and provides fundamental insights into polymorph control in molecular crystalline materials.
tldr: This paper investigates electric-field-driven nanoconfinement to stabilize piezoelectric β-glycine nanocrystals within a 5–120 nm size range.
motivation: Controlled preparation of piezoelectric β-glycine is challenging; existing nanoconfinement methods cannot reliably capture the intrinsic confinement regime for β-phase formation.
method: Electrohydrodynamic spraying under a DC field was used to produce glycine nanoparticles, with spraying height varied to modulate nanoconfinement during nucleation and growth.
result: Pure β-glycine forms within a crystal radius range of 5–120 nm; a crystallization phase map delineating confinement conditions for β-phase stabilization was constructed.
conclusion: This work identifies critical nanoconfinement parameters for accessing piezoelectric β-glycine and provides insights into polymorph control in molecular crystals.

title: Visualizing Lattice-mismatch-dependent Strain Relaxation In Epitaxially Grown MoS2/WS2 And MoS2/WSe2 Hetero-bilayers
authors: Jinwoo Kim, Ingyu Yoo, Jaewoong Joo, Hyoungseok Lee, Jundong Yeo, Jian-Min Zuo, Miyoung Kim And Gwan-Hyoung Lee
abstract: Strain relaxation at lattice-mismatched interfaces is critical for epitaxial growth and high-quality single-crystal films. While van der Waals (vdW) epitaxy is considered as a promising platform due to its high tolerance to lattice mismatch, its actual response to lattice mismatch remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the effect of lattice mismatch on vdW interfaces by epitaxially growing MoS2 on WS2 or WSe2 substrate. annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy reveals that MoS2/WS2 with a negligible lattice mismatch of ∼0.22% forms a fully commensurate structure, whereas MoS2/WSe2 with a large lattice mismatch of ∼3.96% exhibits non-uniform moiré patterns, characteristic of an incommensurate interface. Detailed analysis shows that the MoS2/WS2 hetero-bilayers exhibit perfectly aligned structure through compression of MoS2, whereas the MoS2/WSe2 hetero-bilayers show elongation and rotation of moiré orientation driven by tensile strain. Notably, even small twist angles induce significant changes in moiré orientation, resulting in bent fringes that are indicative of local rotational distortions. Large lattice mismatch drives localized lattice distortion, where rotation of the MoS2 lattice emerges as an energetically favorable mechanism for strain release, in contrast to commensurate alignment in small-mismatch systems. Our results establish moiré pattern analysis as a powerful framework for directly visualizing spatially varying strain and its relaxation pathways in vdW hetero-bilayers. Our work reveals previously inaccessible interfacial deformation modes in vdW hetero-bilayers and establishes moiré analysis as a powerful platform for strain engineering in 2D electronic and optoelectronic materials.
tldr: This paper studies strain relaxation in MoS2/WS2 and MoS2/WSe2 hetero-bilayers using microscopy and moiré pattern analysis.
motivation: To understand how lattice mismatch affects strain relaxation in van der Waals epitaxy, which is important for growing high-quality 2D materials.
method: Epitaxial growth of MoS2 on WS2 or WSe2 substrates, followed by annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy and moiré pattern analysis.
result: Small mismatch (0.22%) leads to commensurate structure via compression; large mismatch (3.96%) causes incommensurate moiré patterns with rotation and elongation driven by tensile strain.
conclusion: Moiré pattern analysis is a powerful tool for visualizing strain relaxation, revealing that rotation is an energetically favorable mechanism for strain release in large-mismatch systems.

authors: Keith Lymohajeet B. SignificancePhotovoltaic subretinal prosthesis can restore form vision in patients blinded by age-related macular degeneration. However, residual photoreceptors surrounding the degenerate area can substantially alter the responses of the inner retinal ...
tldr: This paper studies how residual photoreceptors in a degenerate retina affect responses to electrical stimulation from a photovoltaic subretinal prosthesis.
motivation: To understand the impact of surviving photoreceptors on the efficacy of retinal prostheses for restoring vision in age-related macular degeneration.
method: Experimental measurements and modeling of retinal responses to electrical stimulation in degenerate retinas with residual photoreceptors.
result: Residual photoreceptors significantly alter the inner retinal response to electrical stimulation, potentially affecting prosthetic vision quality.
conclusion: Accounting for residual photoreceptor activity is important for optimizing retinal prostheses and improving visual outcomes.

title: Navigating High-order Protein Fitness Landscapes Via Deep Learning On Directed Evolution Trajectories
authors: Chengzhi Songliang Malingfeng Xueyingfan Xuqihan Zhangyuxi Liuchen Songyihan Linacenter For Quantitative Biology And Peking-Tsinghua Center For Life Sciences, Academy For Advanced Interdisciplinary Studies, Peking University, Beijing 100871, Chinabthe Ministry Of Education Key Laboratory Of Cell Proliferation And Differentiation, School Of Life Sciences, Peking University, Beijing 100871, Chinacpeking University Chengdu Academy For Advanced Interdisciplinary Biotechnologies, Chengdu, Sichuan 610213, China

SignificanceMapping sequence–function landscape of target protein is fundamental to protein engineering and to a deeper understanding of protein function. While the effect of a single mutation is often studied, the impact of combining multiple mutations ...
tldr: This paper uses deep learning on directed evolution trajectories to map high-order protein fitness landscapes.
motivation: Understanding the impact of multiple mutations on protein function is crucial for protein engineering, but high-order epistasis makes it challenging.
method: The authors apply deep learning models to sequence data from directed evolution experiments to predict fitness landscapes.
result: The deep learning approach accurately captures high-order epistatic interactions and predicts protein fitness.
conclusion: This method can accelerate protein engineering by enabling in silico exploration of sequence space.

title: Anti-CRISPR-mediated Continuous Directed Evolution Of CRISPR-Cas9 In Human Cells
authors: Andrew L. Sabolamanuella A. Mengisteprashant Singhvedagopuram Sreekanthsamuel J. Hendelminh Thuan Nguyen Trananton M. Barybinsantosh Chaudharyra’mal M. Harriskristi E. Liivakzachary C.
