tldr: This paper presents a method for continuous directed evolution of CRISPR-Cas9 in human cells using anti-CRISPR proteins.
motivation: To engineer CRISPR-Cas9 variants with improved function in human cells, as most directed evolution is done in bacteria which may not translate to human cellular environments.
method: The authors developed a system using anti-CRISPR proteins to inhibit Cas9 activity, coupled with a mutagenesis strategy to evolve Cas9 variants that evade inhibition, thereby selecting for improved DNA recognition and activity in human cells.
result: They successfully evolved Cas9 variants with enhanced DNA recognition and resistance to anti-CRISPR proteins, demonstrating the feasibility of continuous directed evolution in human cells.
conclusion: This approach enables the engineering of CRISPR tools directly in human cells, potentially leading to more effective gene editing therapies and a better understanding of Cas9 function in complex environments.

title: Universal Deformations And Universal Residual Stresses In Incompressible Isotropic Cauchy Elasticity
authors: Arash Yavari
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study universal deformations in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids with residual stress, without assuming any specific origin for the residual stress. Starting from the constitutive representation of the Cauchy stress as an isotropic tensor-valued function of strain and residual stress, we derive the universality constraints for residually-stressed incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids. We show that for the six known families of universal deformations the set of universal deformations is identical to that of incompressible isotropic elasticity in the absence of residual stress. We also show that residual stress does not enlarge the space of universal deformations. We then determine the universal residual stress fields corresponding to the six known families of universal deformations. Assuming that the residual stress field has the same symmetry as the corresponding universal deformation, the universality constraints reduce to systems of ordinary differential equations that can be solved explicitly. The resulting universal residual stress fields are characterized and discussed for each family.
tldr: This paper studies universal deformations and residual stresses in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how residual stress affects universal deformations in nonlinear elasticity, without assuming a specific origin for the residual stress.
method: Derives universality constraints from constitutive representation of Cauchy stress as isotropic function of strain and residual stress, then solves systems of ODEs for six known families of universal deformations.
result: The set of universal deformations is identical to that without residual stress; residual stress does not enlarge the space. Universal residual stress fields are characterized for each family.
conclusion: Provides a complete classification of universal residual stress fields, which may be useful in nonlinear elasticity theory but has no direct application to the user's research interests.

title: Counting Votes With Multisets
authors: Bart Jacobs, Michael Johnson, Richard Buckland
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A multiset is a 'set' in which elements may occur multiple times. These structures are ideal for expressing the outcome of an election, for instance of the form 60 'yes' and 40 'no'. Moreover, multisets are a useful datatype in vote counting algorithms. This will be illustrated in three different forms of vote counting, known as: 'instant-runoff', 'De Borda', and 'single transferrable vote'. The relevant abstract properties of multisets are: (1) they form a (free) commutative monoid, and (2) they form a functor, and (3) also a monad. This paper illustrates how such categorical properties can be put to good use in deriving and expressing election outcomes. The emphasis is not on the (elementary) category theory involved, but on its application in voting systems.
tldr: This paper uses multisets and category theory to model and analyze three voting systems, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To demonstrate the utility of multisets and their categorical properties in vote counting algorithms.
method: The authors apply the abstract properties of multisets (commutative monoid, functor, monad) to derive and express outcomes of instant-runoff, De Borda, and single transferable vote systems.
result: The paper shows how categorical structures can simplify and generalize vote counting procedures.
conclusion: The work is a contribution to applied category theory and voting theory, with no implications for quantum computing or thermodynamics.

title: N-ary Quasi-arithmetic Means And Families Without Regularity
authors: Ekaterina Shulman Gergely Kiss
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical theorems of Kolmogorov--Nagumo--de Finetti and of Aczel--Maksa characterize quasi-arithmetic means from two complementary directions: the former for compatible families of means satisfying the replacement axiom, and the latter for bisymmetric means of fixed arity. We refine both representation results by showing that the required continuity follows automatically. Our main result states that every reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric and partially strictly increasing [MATH]-variable operation on a real interval is continuous and hence quasi-arithmetic. The proof is based on a recursive construction on [MATH]-adic rationals given by bisymmetry, and a dense-domain continuity argument. The same method also yields the regularity-free Kolmogorov--Nagumo--de Finetti theorem for compatible families of strictly increasing symmetric means.
tldr: The paper proves that continuity follows from algebraic axioms for quasi-arithmetic means, removing regularity assumptions from classical theorems.
motivation: To refine classical representation theorems for quasi-arithmetic means by showing that continuity is not an independent assumption but a consequence of other axioms.
method: Uses a recursive construction on n-adic rationals based on bisymmetry and a dense-domain continuity argument.
result: Every reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric and partially strictly increasing operation on a real interval is continuous and hence quasi-arithmetic; similar result for compatible families of means.
conclusion: The results strengthen the foundations of mean theory, but the paper is purely mathematical and unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or condensed matter.

title: Some Properties Of Besov-Morrey Type Spaces
authors: A. Ussentay, K. Sadykova, N. Tleukhanova
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers Sobolev-Morrey and Besov-Morrey spaces. For Morrey spaces, multipliers are studied, and a theorem on multipliers from M_p^lambda(T) to M_p^lambda(T) is obtained for 1 < p < infinity and 0 <= lambda < 1/p. Based on this result, embeddings between Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-type spaces are established, namely B_1^alpha(M_p^lambda) embedded into W^alpha(M_p^lambda) embedded into B_infinity^alpha(M_p^lambda) for 0 < p <= infinity, 0 <= lambda <= 1/p, and alpha in R. In addition, an interpolation theorem for Besov-Morrey spaces is proved.
tldr: This paper studies embeddings and interpolation theorems for Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-Morrey function spaces.
motivation: To extend classical function space theory to Morrey-type spaces, which are useful in PDEs and harmonic analysis.
method: Analytical proofs using multiplier theorems and embedding techniques for function spaces on the torus.
result: Established embeddings between Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-Morrey spaces, and proved an interpolation theorem for Besov-Morrey spaces.
conclusion: Provides foundational results for further study of function spaces, but no direct application to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Reverse Inequalities For super-Riesz Transforms On Graphs With A Slow Diffusion
authors: Joseph Feneuil
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the [MATH]-dimensional Vicsek graph, we prove that the Riesz-like inequality [MATH] holds for every [MATH] and every [MATH] while it fails whenever [MATH] and [MATH]. Thus, the validity of the inequality remains open only at the critical exponent [MATH]. This provides the first example of an [MATH]-bounded ``super-Riesz transform'', namely an operator of the form [MATH] with [MATH] strictly larger than the Euclidean threshold [MATH]. To achieve this, we establish a more general result linking the diffusion escape rate and a Poincar\'e inequality on balls to the validity of the reverse Riesz-like inequality [MATH].
tldr: This paper proves reverse inequalities for super-Riesz transforms on Vicsek graphs, establishing a new example of an Lp-bounded super-Riesz transform with p>2.
motivation: To understand the validity of reverse Riesz-like inequalities on graphs with slow diffusion, particularly at critical exponents.
method: The authors link diffusion escape rate and Poincaré inequality on balls to the validity of the reverse inequality, and analyze the Vicsek graph as a specific example.
result: The reverse inequality holds for all p and q when p<2, fails when p>2 and q>2, and remains open at p=2.
conclusion: This provides the first example of an Lp-bounded super-Riesz transform with p>2, but the work is purely mathematical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: On Parallel And Batch-Cutting Strategies For Norm-Minimization-Based Convex Vector Optimization
authors: Mohammed Alshahrani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop parallel and batch-cutting variants of the norm-minimization-based outer approximation algorithm for convex vector optimization. The standard algorithm solves [MATH] independent subproblems at each iteration~[MATH] to evaluate all vertices of the current polyhedral approximation, but processes only the single best cut. We propose two improvements. First, we parallelize the across [MATH] workers, reducing per-iteration wall-clock time. Second, we introduce a batch-cutting strategy that adds up to [MATH] supporting halfspaces per iteration, using information from all solved subproblems rather than discarding it. We prove that the batch-cutting variant inherits the convergence rate [MATH] of the standard algorithm, where [MATH] is the number of outer iterations and [MATH] is the number of objectives. Computational experiments on eight test problems with [MATH] show that parallelism on 8 cores , and batch cutting consistently reduces the iteration count by 62--80\%. However, the wall-clock benefit of batch cutting is problem-dependent: the additional cuts per iteration accelerate vertex count growth, so batch cutting is most effective when per-vertex subproblem cost dominates.
tldr: This paper proposes parallel and batch-cutting strategies for norm-minimization-based convex vector optimization, improving computational efficiency.
motivation: To reduce the wall-clock time and iteration count of the standard norm-minimization-based outer approximation algorithm for convex vector optimization.
method: Parallelizes subproblem evaluation across workers and introduces a batch-cutting strategy that adds multiple supporting halfspaces per iteration using information from all solved subproblems.
result: Parallelism on 8 cores and batch cutting reduce iteration count by 62-80%, but wall-clock benefit of batch cutting depends on per-vertex subproblem cost.
conclusion: The batch-cutting variant inherits the convergence rate of the standard algorithm, and its effectiveness varies with problem characteristics.

title: Derivations Of Rational Vertex Operator Algebras Are Inner
authors: Jianzhi Han
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every derivation of a simple and rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type is an inner derivation.
tldr: This paper proves that all derivations of simple rational vertex operator algebras of CFT type are inner derivations.
motivation: To understand the structure of derivations in vertex operator algebras, which is important for the theory of vertex algebras and their representations.
method: Algebraic and representation-theoretic techniques within the framework of vertex operator algebras.
result: Every derivation of a simple rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type is inner.
conclusion: This result clarifies the derivation algebra of such vertex algebras, with implications for their automorphism groups and deformation theory.

title: Policy-Compliant Cloud Storage Systems
authors: Dimitrios Stavrakakis, Masanori Misono, Julian Pritzi, Harshavardhan Unnibhavi, Nuno Santos, Pramod Bhatotia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Privacy regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) impose strict requirements on how personal data is stored, processed, and audited. While key-value stores (KVS) are widely used in latency-sensitive applications, their simple data model and untrusted cloud deployment environments make GDPR compliance particularly challenging. Existing approaches require invasive code modifications, impose high performance overheads, or overlook the integrity of compliance mechanisms themselves. This paper presents GDPRuler, a trusted middleware system that enables verifiable GDPR compliance for KVS on untrusted clouds without modifying their codebase. GDPRuler deploys a trusted GDPR monitor inside a Confidential Virtual Machine (CVM), which enforces GDPR policies, manages compliance metadata, and maintains tamper-evident audit logs. A declarative policy language translates core GDPR obligations into enforceable runtime rules. To ensure efficiency, GDPRuler encodes metadata compactly within KV records, builds dedicated metadata indexes for GDPR-specific queries, and logs only compliance-relevant events in a space-efficient format. We implement GDPRuler as a transparent proxy for unmodified Redis and RocksDB deployments. Evaluation with YCSB and GDPR-inspired workloads shows that GDPRuler enforces core compliance guarantees with low overheads: GDPRuler achieves ~61% of native KVS throughput with the CVM environment contributing 28%-32% of it, metadata storage overhead remains below 20%, and GDPR queries benefit from 13-182x speedup through metadata indexing. By embedding verifiable policy enforcement into a trusted middleware layer, GDPRuler offers a practical path toward GDPR-compliant KVS on untrusted cloud infrastructures.
tldr: GDPRuler is a trusted middleware system that enforces GDPR compliance for key-value stores on untrusted clouds without code modifications.
motivation: Privacy regulations like GDPR impose strict requirements on data storage and processing, but existing key-value stores lack built-in compliance mechanisms and current solutions are invasive or inefficient.
method: GDPRuler deploys a trusted GDPR monitor inside a Confidential Virtual Machine (CVM) that enforces policies, manages metadata, and maintains audit logs; it uses a declarative policy language and compact metadata encoding.
result: GDPRuler achieves ~61% of native KVS throughput with CVM overhead contributing 28-32%, metadata storage overhead below 20%, and 13-182x speedup for GDPR queries via indexing.
conclusion: GDPRuler provides a practical, verifiable compliance layer for KVS on untrusted clouds, with low overhead and no code changes, enabling broader adoption of GDPR-compliant cloud storage.

title: Dimensionality Reduction For Cyberattack Classification: A Comparative Evaluation Of Pca And Linear Predictive Coding
authors: Nelly Elsayed, Zag Elsayed, Navid Asadizanjani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional feature representations are widely used in machine learning-based cyberattack detection systems. However, they increase computational complexity and may hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. In this paper, we investigate feature compression techniques for cyberattack classification by comparing two dimensionality reduction approaches: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Linear Predictive Coding (LPC). Compressed feature representations with varying dimensionalities are generated and evaluated across several classification models. Experimental analysis demonstrates that PCA preserves classification performance even under aggressive compression. On the other hand, LPC provides competitive predictive representations with slightly larger performance degradation. The results show that substantial reductions in feature dimensionality can be achieved with minimal impact on classification accuracy, highlighting the potential of lightweight feature compression for efficient cybersecurity analytics.
tldr: This paper compares PCA and LPC for dimensionality reduction in cyberattack classification, showing that aggressive compression can maintain accuracy.
motivation: High-dimensional features in cyberattack detection increase computational cost, hindering deployment in resource-constrained environments.
method: The authors apply PCA and LPC to compress feature vectors and evaluate classification performance across multiple models.
result: PCA preserves classification performance even under aggressive compression, while LPC shows slightly larger degradation.
conclusion: Substantial dimensionality reduction is possible with minimal accuracy loss, enabling lightweight cybersecurity analytics.

title: Protecting K-Nearest Neighbor Queries From Location Inference Attacks
authors: Zhiyu Sun, Jie Fu, Xinpeng Ling, Huifa Li, Zhili Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The k-nearest neighbor query (kNNQ) is a core component of modern location-based services (LBS) and has been widely adopted in popular features such as ``people nearby''. However, its potential privacy risks have long been overlooked. In this work, we present the first two attacks against kNNQ, namely the geometric intersection location inference attack (GI-LIA) and the zero-order optimization location inference attack (ZO-LIA), revealing the inherent location privacy risks posed by kNNQ. To mitigate these privacy risks, we further propose DPRS, a differential privacy framework for kNNQ protection. The core idea of DPRS is to incorporate a rejection sampling mechanism within a constrained perturbation interval, thereby mitigating the distance distortion caused by excessive noise injection. In addition, we design a private interval construction algorithm to construct the perturbation interval, enabling the rejection sampling mechanism to achieve a more favorable trade-off between privacy protection and query utility in kNNQ. Extensive experiments on real-world spatial datasets demonstrate that DPRS outperforms existing methods in both privacy protection and query utility. Our code is available at [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes attacks and a differential privacy framework for protecting location privacy in k-nearest neighbor queries, with no connection to quantum computing or thermodynamics.
motivation: Location privacy risks in kNN queries have been overlooked; existing methods lack adequate protection.
method: Two location inference attacks (geometric intersection and zero-order optimization) are introduced, and a differential privacy framework with rejection sampling and private interval construction is proposed.
result: The proposed DPRS framework achieves better privacy-utility trade-off than existing methods on real-world datasets.
conclusion: The work highlights privacy vulnerabilities in kNN queries and provides a practical defense mechanism.

title: Cognitive Threat Intelligence And Explainable Federated Security Analytics For Distributed Infrastructure Systems
authors: Md. Arifur Rahman, B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Iqbal Hossan, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing adoption of distributed infrastructure systems, cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, and edge-based architectures has significantly expanded the cybersecurity attack surface and introduced increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. Conventional centralized intrusion detection approaches often face challenges related to scalability, data privacy, communication overhead, and limited transparency in artificial intelligence-driven decision-making processes. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Cognitive Threat Intelligence and Explainable Federated Security Analytics framework for distributed infrastructure systems. The proposed framework integrates Federated Learning (FL), Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and cognitive cybersecurity analytics to enable collaborative and privacy-preserving cyber threat detection across distributed network environments. Instead of transmitting sensitive raw network traffic data to centralized servers, local security models are independently trained at distributed nodes, where only encrypted model parameters and updates are shared through a federated aggregation mechanism. This decentralized learning architecture improves privacy protection while reducing communication dependency and centralized security risks. To enhance intelligent threat analysis, the framework incorporates machine learning and deep learning algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost, Autoencoder.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated learning framework with explainable AI for cybersecurity threat detection in distributed systems, but it is unrelated to quantum computing, information thermodynamics, or quantum foundations.
motivation: The research addresses scalability, privacy, and transparency challenges in centralized intrusion detection for distributed infrastructure systems.
method: The framework integrates Federated Learning (FL), Explainable AI (XAI), and cognitive analytics, using local models trained on distributed nodes with encrypted parameter sharing, and employs algorithms like Random Forest, XGBoost, and Autoencoder.
result: The approach improves privacy protection and reduces communication overhead while enabling collaborative threat detection, though specific performance metrics are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The framework offers a privacy-preserving and transparent security solution for distributed systems, with potential for future integration of more advanced AI techniques.

title: An Embarrassingly Simple Detector For Model Extraction Attacks In Large Language Model Api Traffic
authors: Shuze Liu, Qianwen Guo, Yushun Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed through hosted APIs, making model extraction a practical threat to model ownership and service security. However, individual extraction queries often resemble benign requests, and existing evaluations often focus on single-query anomaly scoring or pure benign-versus-attacker user settings. We formulate model extraction monitoring as benign-calibrated traffic-window distribution testing and show that an embarrassingly simple detector is effective: embed incoming queries into a semantic space and test whether their aggregate distribution deviates from historical benign traffic. We instantiate the detector with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), using only benign-vs-benign comparisons to set the decision threshold. We evaluate on fourteen attacker-normal query pairs from four extraction scenarios and compare with adapted PRADA, SEAT, CAP, DATE, and marginal Mahalanobis baselines. Across three random seeds, MMD achieves 0.3% benign FPR, 100.0% pure-attacker TPR, 90.5% average TPR over attacker fractions, and 95.1% balanced accuracy. These results show that benign-calibrated distribution testing is a strong empirical baseline for model extraction detection in both user-level and mixed multi-user LLM API traffic. Code is released at: [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a simple detector for model extraction attacks on LLM APIs using distribution testing with MMD.
motivation: Model extraction attacks threaten LLM service security, but existing detection methods are complex or focus on single queries.
method: The detector embeds queries into a semantic space and uses maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to compare the distribution of incoming traffic against historical benign traffic, with thresholds set using benign-vs-benign comparisons.
result: The MMD detector achieves 0.3% benign FPR, 100% pure-attacker TPR, 90.5% average TPR, and 95.1% balanced accuracy across multiple attack scenarios.
conclusion: Benign-calibrated distribution testing is a strong baseline for model extraction detection in LLM API traffic, with potential for further refinement.

title: Membrane: A Self-Evolving Contrastive Safety Memory For Llm Agent Defense
authors: Minseok Choi, Seungbin Yang, Dongjin Kim, Subin Kim, Jungmin Son, Yunseung Lee, Jaegul Choo, Youngjun Kwak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite advances in safety alignment, large language models remain vulnerable to continuously evolving jailbreaks. Existing fine-tuned safety classifiers cannot adapt to these evolving attacks, while adaptive memory-based guardrails tend to over-refuse benign queries that resemble stored attacks. We propose Membrane, a self-evolving guardrail built on Contrastive Safety Memory (CSM): each cell pairs the conditions for blocking a harmful query with those for permitting a superficially similar benign request. Without retraining, Membrane evolves CSM by distilling each harmful interaction and its benign counterpart into a contrastive cell indexed by the underlying attack strategy, so that one cell generalizes across topical variants of the same mechanism. At inference, retrieved cells serve as grounding context for precise safety decisions. Across model-level safety on HarmBench and agent-level safety on AgentHarm, Membrane achieves the highest F1 on all six jailbreak attacks. Notably, benign refusal on AgentHarm stays at 7-14%, well below the 28-85% range of prior guards. Memory cells also retain 87-88% F1 under cross-attack transfer and remain stable under memory poisoning.
tldr: Membrane is a self-evolving guardrail for LLM agents that uses contrastive safety memory to defend against jailbreak attacks without retraining.
motivation: Existing safety classifiers cannot adapt to evolving jailbreaks, and memory-based guardrails over-refuse benign queries.
method: Contrastive Safety Memory stores pairs of harmful and benign queries; at inference, retrieved cells provide context for safety decisions, and the memory evolves by distilling new attacks into contrastive cells.
result: Membrane achieves highest F1 on HarmBench and AgentHarm across six jailbreak attacks, with benign refusal rates of 7-14% compared to 28-85% for prior methods.
conclusion: The approach offers adaptive, low-overhead defense for LLM agents, with potential for cross-attack generalization and robustness to memory poisoning.

title: SentinelRAG: Synthetic Sentinel Knowledge For Rag Database Copyright Protection
authors: Tsun On Kwok, Xi Yang, Ki Sen Hung, Chang Liu, Yangqiu Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protecting proprietary RAG databases from unauthorized redistribution is challenging: existing watermarking methods either inject fabricated relations between real entities, polluting the knowledge base with misinformation, or embed fragile lexical patterns that adversarial paraphrasing easily removes. We propose SentinelRAG, a watermarking framework that embeds style-consistent but fictitious knowledge entries into the RAG database. Our key insight is that synthetic knowledge describing fictitious entities is unlikely to be retrieved by legitimate queries, yet can be reliably triggered through targeted probes known only to the data owner. Experiments on four datasets ranging from 2.9k to 8.8M documents demonstrate that SentinelRAG achieves statistically significant detection [MATH] across all tested configurations at only a 0.1% injection rate. Compared to the state-of-the-art, our method significantly reduces the false detection rate while maintaining negligible interference with legitimate user queries.
tldr: SentinelRAG is a watermarking framework for protecting RAG databases by injecting fictitious knowledge entries that are detectable via targeted probes.
motivation: Existing watermarking methods for RAG databases either pollute the knowledge base with misinformation or are vulnerable to adversarial paraphrasing.
method: The method embeds style-consistent but fictitious knowledge entries describing nonexistent entities into the RAG database, which are unlikely to be retrieved by legitimate queries but can be triggered by specific probes.
result: Experiments on four datasets (2.9k to 8.8M documents) show statistically significant detection at only 0.1% injection rate, with reduced false detection rate and negligible interference with legitimate queries.
conclusion: SentinelRAG offers a robust and low-impact watermarking solution for copyright protection of RAG databases, with potential for further optimization and deployment.

title: Exploring The Connection Between Coding Habits And Cognitive Styles In Malware Developers
authors: Vasilis Vouvoutsis, Constantinos Patsakis, Fran Casino
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Malware research primarily studies the results, the methods, and the impact. Even from an offensive security perspective, what is examined is the method, not the development strategy of the offender. This study investigates the behavioral signatures and coding patterns embedded in the malware source code. By analyzing a large corpus of leaked malware code and comparing it with carefully selected benign open-source software, we apply static application security testing and compute multiple software metrics. Based on cognitive psychology and criminological theories, our work interprets differences in code structure and quality as behavioral indicators, reflecting distinct motivational structures, risk tolerances, and development strategies of malware authors compared to benign software developers. Our findings reveal that malware code is generally smaller, less documented, and exhibits higher cyclomatic complexity per function, with reduced use of abstraction mechanisms such as classes and closures. Vulnerability analysis further reveals that malware exhibits more issues of the types that benign code typically avoids, suggesting a minimal investment in secure development practices. These patterns imply a development style optimized for expedience, operational secrecy, and evasion rather than long-term maintainability. Nonetheless, the code quality metrics indicate that it does not deviate significantly from benign software enough to be distinctive. By framing code metrics as proxies for behavioral signals and strategic choices, we demonstrate how quantitative software analysis can enrich behavioral cybersecurity research, offering new insights into the practices and priorities of malware developers. Our results pave the way for further research in the behavioral profiling of cyber offenders.
tldr: This paper analyzes coding patterns in malware source code to infer behavioral traits of malware developers, using software metrics and cognitive psychology.
motivation: To understand the behavioral signatures and development strategies of malware authors compared to benign developers, moving beyond traditional malware analysis.
method: Applied static application security testing and computed software metrics on a large corpus of leaked malware code and benign open-source software, interpreting differences through cognitive psychology and criminological theories.
result: Malware code is smaller, less documented, has higher cyclomatic complexity per function, and fewer abstractions; it also exhibits more security issues, suggesting expedience and evasion over maintainability.
conclusion: Quantitative software analysis can enrich behavioral cybersecurity research, offering insights into malware developers' practices and priorities, but code quality differences are not extreme enough to be distinctive.

title: Double-Directional Wireless Channel Modeling Using Statistics-Aided Machine Learning
authors: Ferdous Pervej Richmond Boamah
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The double-directional (DD) wireless channel model is important for realistic system design since it provides complete propagation information. While stochastic and deterministic channel models are widely adopted, and existing machine learning (ML) solutions mostly aim to align future channel realizations, these solutions are often limited to short time spans that may not be statistically significant. Moreover, because the number of multi-path components (MPCs) varies with spatial and temporal variation of the receiver (RX) and/or interacting objects (IOs), typical ML solutions that require fixed, predefined input and output shapes fall short. To curb these limitations, we propose a statistics-aided ML solution that relies on a fixed subset of MPCs selection. More specifically, we first select top-[MATH] MPCs, where [MATH] is much smaller than the total number of MPCs, and construct learnable graphs to train our proposed hybrid TimesNet-TimeFilter (TNTF) model. We then use a channel statistics-aided training method to generate future top-M DD channel realizations such that the statistics calculated from these realizations matches closely with those of the actual statistics from the complete time-varying DD channel realizations. We validate the proposed solution using extensive simulations on both synthetic stochastic channel model (SCM)-based and deterministic ray-tracing-based datasets, and demonstrate its effectiveness relative to state-of-the-art baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes a statistics-aided machine learning model for double-directional wireless channel modeling, focusing on multi-path component selection and time-series prediction.
motivation: Existing ML solutions for channel modeling are limited to short time spans and require fixed input/output shapes, failing to handle varying numbers of multi-path components.
method: The authors select a fixed subset of top-M multi-path components, construct learnable graphs, and train a hybrid TimesNet-TimeFilter model using channel statistics to generate future channel realizations.
result: The proposed method matches the statistics of actual time-varying double-directional channel realizations and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on synthetic and ray-tracing datasets.
conclusion: The work provides a practical ML approach for long-term channel modeling, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is negligible.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews advances in geospace science achieved using the Arecibo Observatory's radar, lidar, and optical instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: To summarize key scientific contributions from the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research over its 50-year operation.
method: Review of incoherent scatter radar technique and synthesis of results from Arecibo's suite of instruments including lidars and optical sensors.
result: The paper highlights advances in plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory enabled unique observations of geospace phenomena, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews convection-cloud chambers as a tool to study the bottleneck in warm rain formation, focusing on condensation and collision coalescence.
motivation: To address the long-standing theoretical difficulty in explaining the rapid transition from condensation to collision coalescence in warm clouds.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and computational studies on convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud microphysics under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can capture turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The approach offers a promising path to resolve the precipitation bottleneck, with implications for cloud physics and climate modeling.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in ground-based interferometers.
motivation: To summarize progress in modeling core collapse supernovae and predicting gravitational wave signals for multimessenger astronomy.
method: Review of core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, along with detection methods for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: Latest progress in supernova modeling and associated gravitational wave signal predictions are presented.
conclusion: Detection of gravitational waves from a near-Galactic supernova would provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a tension between the dipole in the cosmic microwave background and that in large-scale structure, which challenges the cosmological principle and the ΛCDM model.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by comparing the dipole in the CMB with that in radio galaxy and quasar catalogs.
method: Statistical analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in the matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The anomaly may challenge the standard ΛCDM model, and further investigation of biases and alternate interpretations is needed.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This review covers the fluid dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, focusing on turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: To understand the complex behavior of gas bubbles in various natural and industrial processes, and to improve modeling of two-phase flows.
method: Review of recent advances (past 20 years) in experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of bubble dynamics.
result: Key factors affecting bubble motion include added mass, deformability, turbulence, liquid rheology, surfactants, and interactions with walls and other bubbles.
conclusion: The review provides insights for enhancing models of two-phase flow systems and suggests future research directions in turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.

title: The Euclidean Algorithm, Lotuses And Singularities
authors: Patrick Popescu-Pampu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The anthyphairetic process leads from a pair (a,b) of coprime positive integers to the pair (1,1) by successive subtractions of the smaller number from the bigger one. This process, which is a slow version of Euclid's algorithm applied to the pair (a,b), corresponds naturally to the process of successive blowups leading to the minimal embedded resolution of the plane curve defined by y^a - x^b = 0. This blowup process may be represented graphically by a special two-dimensional simplicial complex called a lotus. This allows to localize the various numbers appearing either during the anthyphairetic process or during the Euclidean algorithm at precise positions inside the lotus. In this introductory article, I recall first the construction of this lotus starting from the sequence of quotients generated by the Euclidean algorithm. I present then an alternative way of constructing it directly from the sequence of pairs of coprime integers generated by the anthyphairetic process, using what I call anthyphairetic rectangles. I conclude by explaining how to reconstruct from a lotus the corresponding sequence of pairs of coprime integers. This is a simple illustration of the way lotuses may serve as computational architectures.
tldr: This paper explores a geometric representation of the Euclidean algorithm using lotuses and its connection to resolution of singularities of plane curves.
motivation: To provide a visual and combinatorial interpretation of the Euclidean algorithm and anthyphairetic process, linking number theory to algebraic geometry.
method: The paper constructs a two-dimensional simplicial complex (lotus) from the sequence of quotients in the Euclidean algorithm, and also from anthyphairetic rectangles, then shows how to recover the original coprime pairs.
result: The lotus construction localizes numbers from the Euclidean algorithm and anthyphairetic process, and the paper presents an alternative construction using anthyphairetic rectangles.
conclusion: Lotuses serve as computational architectures for understanding the Euclidean algorithm and its geometric implications, with potential applications in algebraic geometry.

title: Introduction To Measure And Integration Theory
authors: Hugo Guadalupe Reyna-Casta\~neda, Mar\'ia de Los \'angeles Sandoval-Romero, Luis Antonio Cede\~no-P\'erez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These notes provide a rigorous and accessible introduction to measure and integration theory, with emphasis on the conceptual transition from the Riemann integral to the Lebesgue integral and the role played by limiting processes in modern analysis. The manuscript develops the basic theory of measurable sets, measurable functions, measures on [MATH]-algebras, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, and [MATH] spaces. Particular attention is devoted to the interaction between integration and convergence, as well as to the limitations of the Riemann integral that motivate the development of measure theory. The exposition seeks to balance mathematical rigor with pedagogical clarity through detailed proofs, examples, exercises, and supplementary projects. These notes are intended primarily for undergraduate students in mathematics and related areas encountering measure theory for the first time, although they may also serve as a reference for introductory graduate courses in analysis.
tldr: This paper is a pedagogical introduction to measure and integration theory, covering Lebesgue integration and convergence theorems.
motivation: To provide a rigorous yet accessible introduction to measure theory for undergraduate students, bridging the gap from Riemann to Lebesgue integration.
method: The paper develops measure theory through definitions, theorems, proofs, examples, and exercises, focusing on measurable sets, functions, measures, and Lebesgue integration.
result: The notes present a comprehensive treatment of measure and integration theory, emphasizing convergence theorems and the limitations of the Riemann integral.
conclusion: The work serves as a textbook for students new to measure theory, with no novel research contributions.

title: The {\alpha} -Discounting ({\alpha}-DMCDM) As An Extension Of Ahp, Topsis, Vikor, Promethee, And Weighted Sum
authors: Florentin Smarandache
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and other classic Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) techniques excel when decision makers can provide consistent pair wise judgments. Real world problems, however, often involve inconsistent, n-wise, or non-linear preference structures that render traditional methods inadequate. The {\alpha}-Discounting MCDM ({\alpha}-D MCDM) extends AHP by embedding a global discounting parameter {\alpha} that transforms an inconsistent system of preference equations into a solvable algebraic system.
tldr: This paper extends classic MCDM methods with an α-discounting parameter to handle inconsistent preferences, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Classic MCDM methods like AHP require consistent pairwise judgments, which are often unrealistic in real-world problems with inconsistent or non-linear preferences.
method: The α-Discounting MCDM (α-D MCDM) introduces a global discounting parameter α that transforms an inconsistent system of preference equations into a solvable algebraic system.
result: The method extends AHP, TOPSIS, VIKOR, PROMETHEE, and weighted sum to handle inconsistent preferences.
conclusion: The approach improves decision-making under inconsistency but has no connection to quantum computing, thermodynamics, or the user's research interests.

title: The Ize Conjecture Redux: A Parity Criterion For Global Equivariant Bifurcation Guarantees
authors: Ziad Ghanem
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Ize Conjecture proposed that every absolutely irreducible representation of a compact Lie group admits a maximal isotropy subgroup with an odd-dimensional fixed-point space, which would provide a universal bifurcation guarantee via the equivariant degree. Its disproof by Lauterbach and Matthews necessitates a more targeted criterion. We introduce Ize pairs -- pairs [MATH] for which some maximal isotropy subgroup [MATH] satisfies [MATH] -- and prove that this dimension-parity condition completely captures the algebraic obstruction to a non-trivial equivariant degree change at maximal orbit types. Integrating this criterion with a mod-2 equivariant spectral flow yields local and global bifurcation guarantees without recourse to Burnside ring arithmetic. As an application, we establish unbounded branches of non-stationary periodic solutions in a [MATH]-symmetric coupled oscillator network, where the bifurcation guarantees follow entirely from the crossing parity of the linearization at the boundary of a regular parameter window.
tldr: The paper proves a parity criterion for global equivariant bifurcation in symmetric dynamical systems, with an application to coupled oscillator networks.
motivation: The Ize Conjecture was disproven, so a new criterion is needed to guarantee bifurcations in equivariant systems.
method: Introduces Ize pairs and uses mod-2 equivariant spectral flow to derive local and global bifurcation guarantees.
result: A dimension-parity condition on maximal isotropy subgroups completely captures the algebraic obstruction to nontrivial equivariant degree change.
conclusion: The criterion yields bifurcation guarantees without Burnside ring arithmetic, demonstrated on a D4-symmetric oscillator network.

title: Unique Ergodicity Of Branched Covers Of Translation Surfaces
authors: Elizaveta Shuvaeva Polina Baron
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a finite-area translation surface whose vertical flow is uniquely ergodic. Given a slit joining two nonsingular points of [MATH], one can form a branched cyclic cover by gluing [MATH] copies of [MATH] crosswise along the slit. We study when the vertical flow on the resulting cover is uniquely ergodic. We first prove a geometric criterion for unique ergodicity of the branched cover. We show that if, for a sequence of times along the Teichm\"uller geodesic, one endpoint of the slit is contained in embedded Euclidean disks of uniformly positive radius that avoid the other endpoint, then the branched cover is uniquely ergodic. The proof uses the special symmetry of the cover together with an analysis of forward and backward generic points for the vertical flow. We then show that this criterion applies for Lebesgue-almost every choice of slit endpoint under a natural geometric hypothesis on the Teichm\"uller orbit of [MATH], namely a uniform lower bound for the embedded radius along a subsequence. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for such a lower bound in terms of the cylinder geometry of [MATH], introducing the notion of pipe cylinders and proving that embedded disks of definite size must exist. As a consequence, for the class of uniquely ergodic translation surfaces, almost every slit produces a uniquely ergodic branched [MATH]-cover.
tldr: This paper studies unique ergodicity of vertical flows on branched cyclic covers of translation surfaces, a topic in dynamical systems and Teichmüller theory.
motivation: To understand when the vertical flow on a branched cover of a uniquely ergodic translation surface remains uniquely ergodic, extending known results for unbranched covers.
method: The authors prove a geometric criterion involving embedded Euclidean disks along the Teichmüller geodesic, and show it holds for almost every slit under a uniform lower bound on embedded radius, using the notion of pipe cylinders.
result: For a uniquely ergodic translation surface, almost every choice of slit produces a uniquely ergodic branched cyclic cover.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric condition for unique ergodicity of branched covers and opens questions about the prevalence of such covers in moduli space.

title: Weighted hp-Uniform Decompositions For H^k-Type Tensor-Product Spaces In Arbitrary Dimension
authors: Weiying Zheng Situan Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish weighted hp-uniform vertex-patch decompositions in arbitrary space dimension d >= 1 for tensor-product discretizations of H^k-type conforming and nonconforming spaces, with arbitrary fixed Sobolev order k >= 1, on fitted interface meshes. The cells are coordinate-compatible cuboids, the local spaces are Q_{p_K}(K) with arbitrary elementwise degrees satisfying p_K >= 2k-1, and the coefficient may have arbitrarily large jumps across material interfaces. Under local coefficient oscillation bounds and a local high-side connectivity condition, both the conforming H^k space and the nonconforming spaces V_h^{(s)}, 0 <= s <= k, admit stable decompositions with constants which may depend on the fixed parameters d and k, but are independent of the mesh size, all polynomial degrees, neighboring degree ratios, and the global coefficient contrast. The argument combines a Hermite endpoint transform for endpoint jets of order 0,...,k-1, its tensor-product extension, weighted broken patch Poincare inequalities, and a successive correction of normal derivative jumps. Numerical experiments for a three-dimensional DG problem with large coefficient jumps and strongly varying local polynomial degrees support the predicted robustness. For k = 1 the same conclusions hold on uniformly regular mapped cubical meshes whose neighboring element maps agree on each common face.
tldr: This paper develops weighted hp-uniform decompositions for tensor-product finite element spaces on interface meshes, focusing on numerical analysis and discretization theory.
motivation: To establish stable decompositions for H^k-type conforming and nonconforming spaces with arbitrary polynomial degrees and large coefficient jumps, which are crucial for robust numerical methods.
method: Combines Hermite endpoint transform, tensor-product extension, weighted broken patch Poincaré inequalities, and successive correction of normal derivative jumps.
result: Proved stable decompositions with constants independent of mesh size, polynomial degrees, degree ratios, and coefficient contrast, validated by 3D DG experiments.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical foundation for hp-adaptive methods on interface meshes, with potential extensions to more general meshes and applications.

title: Convergence Rate Of The Halpern Iterations With Possibly Distinct Anchor And Initial Guess
authors: Qiao-Li Dong Jianing He
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All existing convergence rate estimates of Halpern iterations are established only for the case where the anchor coincides with the initial guess. This paper aims to investigate the convergence rate of general Halpern iterations, where the anchor and the initial guess may not necessarily be the same. We present tight convergence rate estimates for both predetermined and adaptive anchoring parameters. These results generalize existing related work.
tldr: This paper studies convergence rates of Halpern iterations with distinct anchor and initial guess, a topic in optimization theory.
motivation: Existing convergence rate estimates for Halpern iterations assume the anchor equals the initial guess; this work generalizes to the case where they differ.
method: The authors analyze both predetermined and adaptive anchoring parameters, deriving tight convergence rate estimates.
result: They provide tight convergence rate estimates for general Halpern iterations, generalizing previous results.
conclusion: The results extend the theory of Halpern iterations, but the paper is purely mathematical and unrelated to the user's research interests.
